prompt: Create one complete production reference atlas for an original 1990s arcade basketball game, exactly 42 DIFFERENT full-body pose drawings, organized in a clean 6-row by 7-column reading order with generous transparent gutters, every pose completely inside its own clear cell. Use genuine transparent RGBA, no floor, no shadows, no glows, no background blocks, no grid lines, no text, no numbers, no ball or props. This is an original canonical athlete, Jennifer, an adult human woman approximately 5 foot 9, with ivory skin, an angular oblong face, deep teal eyes, unmistakable purple wire-rim glasses, long dark chocolate-brown curls worn half-up with small braids and a few feathers. Preserve this identity consistently in all 42 drawings. Strong but lanky athletic build with gentle fullness, normal adult human anatomy. Her court uniform is tasteful forest-green performance sportswear with subtle floral and leaf patterns, restrained bronze fringe at the hems, turquoise necklace and ring, and plain practical open-toe sandals; no robe or staff on court. Intelligent quiet protective expression, never a generic sorceress. Crisp detailed inked anime-arcade sprite art with warm highlights and clean silhouette, matching a 1990s basketball game, same character scale and foot baseline in each cell. Face is angled toward viewer enough that teal eyes and purple wire glasses read clearly at sprite size. Three-quarter body orientation toward screen-right; keep hair, glasses, fingertips, sandal toes inside every cell, with no neighboring poses touching. All 42 poses independently drawn, no duplicated holds. Fill the rows in exact sequence: row1 idle frames 1-6 plus idle-with-ball stance frame1; row2 idle-with-ball frames2-4 then dribble frames1-4; row3 dribble frames5-10 then run frame1; row4 run frames2-8; row5 run frames9-11 then low dribble-run frames1-4; row6 low dribble-run frames5-11. Idle poses breathe and shift weight; ball-ready hands stay empty for the game physics ball; dribble is a distinct low hand cycle with empty hands; run strides alternate legs; dribble-run is a separate low forward sprint with alternating reach. No frame may include a basketball. This is an actual animation sheet, not a menu portrait or concept sheet.
